articles.title: The protests spread to other cities in Italy
articles.description: Protests have spread this Saturday to the main cities of Italy, after a protest last weekend against the rising cost of living and the deterioration of purchasing power degenerated into serious riots and looting in Milan, in the north of the country, and ended with 200 people arrested. On this occasion, there has been a new demonstration in Milan, but also in Rome, Turin, Florence, Naples, and Bologna. All have taken place without serious incidents, but there have been moments of tension. The police have arrested a total of nine people across the country, identified 4,292, and taken 371 to the police station, 110 of whom are minors.

articles.title: The economy wounded by the war also marks Israel's elections
articles.description: The cost of rent, shopping, transport and bills has become one of the main concerns for Israeli families. Four days before the October 27th elections, many are wondering if the next government will be able to ease this pressure after more than three years of war and high military spending. Security remains central to the campaign, but the economy also weighs on the vote. A survey by the research center Israel Democracy Institute (IDI) indicates that the cost of living and the economy are priorities for 38% of Jewish respondents and 46% of Arabs. A malaise that is especially concentrated on the rising cost of housing and food, two structural problems that have been dragging on for years.

articles.title: Are we safe in Europe?
articles.description: The Cold War is a distant memory and a ghost is once again haunting Europe. At least, Western Europe. That of a hot war or, at the very least, a hybrid one, which manifests itself in many ways: sabotage, drones, cyberattacks, the use of immigration as a tool of destabilization... "We have entered a new era of deterrence," predicts security and defense expert Juraj Majcin. Eighty-one years after the defeat of Nazism, the outbreak of a widespread conflict, extending beyond what is now being fought in Ukraine following the invasion by Vladimir Putin's Russia, no longer seems an improbable scenario, and this will be, precisely, one of the topics of the new edition of Enfoquem, next Monday.
